# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

Cation exchange chromatography is the polishing step of the A-Mab purification process and
the last step in the train that changes the aggregate content of the product. It is
operated in bind and elute mode on a strong cation exchange resin, in which the antibody
binds below its isoelectric point and the column is washed at a controlled conductivity.
The product is then eluted by a pH step and collected to a set optical density on the
descending edge of the elution peak. Aggregate carries more positive charge than monomer
and therefore binds more strongly and elutes late, which makes the aggregate content of
the pool depend on how well the two species are resolved and on where the pool is stopped.
Host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A are cleared in the load flow through
and in the wash. No viral clearance claim is made for this step.

This report presents the executed characterization of the step against the approved plan
PCP-007. The studies were run on a qualified scale-down column model of the commercial
process, which is operated at a nominal `{python} f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"` L production scale. Of the `{python} n_params` parameters
carried into the study by RA-001, `{python} n_multi` were studied in a multivariate design and `{python} n_uni`
was assessed one at a time. A two-level full factorial screening design of `{python} n_scr` runs
identified the active factors, after which a face centred central composite design of
`{python} n_rsm` runs provided the predictive models for pool aggregate, pool host cell protein and
step yield.

Protein load has the largest effect on all three responses. In addition, it governs host
cell protein clearance together with the conductivity of the load and wash buffer, and
aggregate clearance together with elution buffer pH and elution stop collect. The
response-surface models explain `{python} f"{100*rsm_r2_lo:.1f}"` % to `{python} f"{100*rsm_r2_hi:.1f}"` % of the variation in their responses,
and none of the three shows significant lack of fit against the centre-point pure error.
Over the characterized region, `{python} pct(DS['fraction'])` of the space meets both in-process criteria, and
aggregate clearance is the binding constraint. Proven acceptable ranges were determined
for each governed attribute against each response-surface factor and are reported in §7.

At commercial scale the step contributes to four drug substance attributes. Simulation of
`{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches with every parameter of the train inside its normal operating range gives a
capability of `{python} f"{cpk('aggregates_hmw'):.1f}"` for aggregate and `{python} f"{cpk('hcp'):.1f}"` for host cell protein, the tightest of the
four attributes this step governs. The tightest capability of the drug substance as a
whole is `{python} f"{V['min_cpk']:.2f}"`, which belongs to a viral clearance attribute that other steps set. Two
deviations were recorded, `{python} n_dev` in total, and both were retained after investigation. The
outcome of this step rolls up into the master report PCMR-001.

# Introduction

## Product and unit operation

A-Mab is a humanized immunoglobulin G monoclonal antibody whose primary mechanism of
action is antibody dependent cell mediated cytotoxicity. It is produced by fed-batch
culture and purified by the Novacyte platform train of Protein A capture, low-pH viral
inactivation, cation exchange chromatography, anion exchange chromatography, small-virus
retentive filtration and ultrafiltration with diafiltration. Cation exchange
chromatography is Step `{python} STEP_NO` of that train, receiving the neutralized pool of the low-pH
viral inactivation step and delivering the load for anion exchange chromatography.

The step is operated in bind and elute mode, in which the load and the wash are held at a
defined conductivity and the product is eluted by a step change in buffer pH. The pool is
collected from the ascending edge of the elution peak to a set optical density on the
descending edge. Two separations happen in different phases of the cycle. Host cell
protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A are acidic at the operating pH, do not bind
the sulfonate ligand and leave in the load flow through and in the wash. Aggregate does
bind, and more strongly than monomer, because a dimer presents twice the charged surface
to the ligand, which is why it elutes behind the monomer. The aggregate the pool carries
is set by the resolution between the two species and by the stop collect point.

The step forms no quality attribute of its own, but it clears four, and for one of them it
is the last opportunity in the process. Because aggregate is formed upstream in the
production bioreactor (Step 3) and is not reduced or generated by any step after cation
exchange, the aggregate content of the pool this step delivers is the aggregate content of
the drug substance. Host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A are cleared
again at anion exchange chromatography (PCR-008). Viral clearance is claimed for the
low-pH inactivation, anion exchange and virus filtration steps, and no clearance is
claimed here.

At the nominal set-point condition the step reduces pool aggregate from `{python} f"{agg_in:.2f}"` % to `{python} f"{agg_out:.2f}"`
% of the total protein, a reduction of `{python} f"{agg_fold:.1f}"`-fold, and reduces host cell protein from
`{python} f"{hcp_in:,.0f}"` ng/mg in the capture pool to `{python} f"{hcp_out:.0f}"` ng/mg, a reduction of `{python} f"{hcp_fold:.0f}"`-fold. Residual DNA
is reduced by `{python} f"{dna_lrv:.1f}"` log₁₀ and leached Protein A by `{python} f"{lpa_lrv:.1f}"` log₁₀, and the step yield is
`{python} pct(yield_nom)`.

## Objectives

The study had five objectives.

- (i) Quantify the relationship between the process parameters of the step and pool
  aggregate, pool host cell protein and step yield, over ranges wider than the intended
  routine ranges.
- (ii) Define the multivariate region over which the step meets the in-process criteria
  for the attributes it governs.
- (iii) Establish a proven acceptable range for each parameter against each governed
  attribute, both at the set-point and with the remaining parameters varying within their
  normal operating ranges.
- (iv) Classify every parameter of the step against the criteria of SOP-4001, from the
  effects the study demonstrates.
- (v) Justify the operating ranges and the in-process controls that this step contributes
  to the control strategy for Stage 2.

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The study is a Stage 1 process design activity in the lifecycle approach to process
validation [@fda2011]. It follows the enhanced development approach of ICH Q8, ICH Q9 and
ICH Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11], in which prior knowledge and a risk assessment
establish what needs to be studied, and designed experiments bound the region within which
the process delivers acceptable quality. Because criticality is treated as a continuum and
not as a binary label [@ichq9], the attributes this step governs carry a graded
criticality and the parameters a graded classification. The process model, the attribute
framework and the risk methodology follow the published A-Mab case study [@amab2009].
Viral safety is evaluated under ICH Q5A [@ichq5a] for the three steps that carry a modular
clearance claim (low-pH inactivation, anion exchange and virus filtration), of which this
step is not one.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Platform and prior-product knowledge

The cation exchange polishing step has been operated on the Novacyte humanized
immunoglobulin platform for three previously licensed antibodies, X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab,
and for the clinical and engineering supply of A-Mab [@amab2009]. The resin, the buffer
system and the mode of operation are unchanged between those products and A-Mab. Because
the platform experience establishes the mechanism of the step and the direction in which
each parameter acts, the purpose of this study was to bound the ranges for A-Mab and not
to discover the behaviour of the step.

Four mechanistic expectations follow from the physical chemistry of the separation and
from that platform experience. Protein load sets the fraction of the ligand in use, and
near capacity both the monomer and the aggregate peaks broaden and overlap, which was
expected to reduce aggregate clearance and to reduce yield at a heavier load. Because the
conductivity of the load and wash buffers sets the ionic strength that shields the charge
on the ligand, a higher conductivity was expected to strip more weakly bound host cell
protein during the wash, while the more strongly bound antibody remains adsorbed. The
elution buffer pH sets the net charge on the antibody at the moment of elution. Therefore,
a higher pH within the range was expected to weaken binding, to bring monomer and
aggregate off closer together and to reduce the resolution on which aggregate clearance
depends. The stop collect point decides how much of the descending edge enters the pool,
and because the aggregate elutes on that edge it is the direct handle on the trade between
aggregate clearance and yield.

Two attributes were expected to be insensitive to the operating parameters. DNA is
strongly negatively charged and is repelled by the cation exchange ligand, which is why it
passes through in the load and why its clearance is a property of the chemistry and not of
any parameter setting. Leached Protein A and its fragments are acidic and do not bind
under the load conditions, while the fraction complexed with the antibody is released when
the complex binds the ligand. Consequently, the step delivers a modest and stable
clearance. Both were measured across the study and neither was carried into the
multivariate design.

## Quality attributes in scope

@tbl-cqa lists the drug substance attributes this step governs, with the acceptance
criterion and the criticality assigned in RA-001. Criticality was assigned by the impact
and uncertainty tool of the A-Mab case study (Tool #1), in which an attribute scored high
or very high is called critical [@amab2009]. Aggregate is the attribute that drives the
study, because it is scored high, its drug substance criterion is `{python} f"{ds_hi(AGG):g}"` % HMW, and this
step is the last one that can reduce it. Host cell protein is scored moderate to high and
is cleared further downstream at anion exchange chromatography. Residual DNA and leached
Protein A are scored very low and low to moderate respectively, and both are cleared by a
wide margin at this step and again at anion exchange.
```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(CQA_KEYS))
```
: Drug substance quality attributes governed by the step. {#tbl-cqa}

The step is judged in this report against its own in-process criteria and not against the
drug substance criteria in @tbl-cqa. An intermediate that carries `{python} f"{hcp_out:.0f}"` ng/mg host cell
protein against a drug substance limit of `{python} f"{ds_hi(HCP):g}"` ng/mg is not a failing intermediate,
because anion exchange chromatography reduces it a further `{python} f"{aex_hcp_fold:.1f}"`-fold. Each in-process
criterion is therefore derived from the drug substance criterion by carrying it back
through the clearance the downstream train delivers and dividing by an assurance factor.
For aggregate no step downstream reduces the attribute, which leaves the ceiling at the
drug substance criterion itself. An assurance factor of `{python} f"{ipc_margin(AGG):g}"` gives an in-process limit
of `{python} f"{ipc_hi(AGG):g}"` % HMW. For host cell protein the ceiling carries back through anion exchange
(Step 8), where an assurance factor of `{python} f"{ipc_margin(HCP):g}"` gives an in-process limit of `{python} f"{ipc_hi(HCP):.0f}"` ng/mg.
Both criteria sit well below the point at which the drug substance would be at risk, which
is what makes them controls and not break-even points.

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection

RA-001 ranked every operating parameter of the step by its potential impact on a quality
attribute and by its potential to interact with other parameters, and assigned each
parameter to a study type on the resulting score. Protein load, wash conductivity, elution
buffer pH and elution stop collect were ranked highest and were carried into the
multivariate design, because each was expected to act on aggregate clearance or on host
cell protein clearance and because the first three were expected to interact. Elution flow
rate was ranked lower and was assigned to a univariate assessment, because within the
range considered and at the particle size of the resin the effect on peak sharpness is
small. Parameters held to platform specification (the buffer composition, the column
packed bed height and the resin lot) were not carried into the study. They are identity
and quality controlled under SOP-2010 and SOP-2008, and were not characterized in this
study.

The ranges carried into the study were widened beyond the intended routine ranges by a
factor of two to three on each parameter, in order to find an edge of failure where one
exists inside a range the process could plausibly reach. The characterization ranges and
the routine ranges are given in @tbl-params.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

The studies were executed on a laboratory-scale packed column model of the commercial
cation exchange step, qualified under SOP-1001. The model uses the same resin, the same
buffer system and the same packed bed height as the commercial column, at the same linear
velocity and at the same load, wash and elution volumes expressed in column volumes.
Column efficiency was matched by plate count and peak asymmetry before each campaign. The
parameters that scale with column diameter, principally the volumetric flow rate and the
absolute load mass, were set to preserve the commercial residence time and the commercial
load in grams of protein per litre of resin.

Model qualification compared the scale-down column with at-scale data (engineering and
clinical manufacture) at the target condition. The comparison covered the input attributes
of the load, the output attributes of the pool and the performance of the separation
itself, which are aggregate, host cell protein, residual DNA, leached Protein A, step
yield and the elution peak volume. No difference was found between scales that the run to
run spread of the at-scale data did not already contain. Therefore, the model is suitable
for defining operating ranges that will be applied at commercial scale, and through that
qualification the claims in this report are made for the commercial step.

The centre-point replicates of each design carry the pure error of the model, with `{python} cp_rsm`
replicates in the response surface design and `{python} cp_scr` in the screening design. Their spread
is the reference against which the lack of fit of each fitted model is tested in §5.3, and
measures the reproducibility of the scale-down system as a whole, including the analytical
methods.

## Operation

Each run followed the cycle defined in SOP-2010. The column was equilibrated in the load
and wash buffer at the conductivity set for that run, loaded to the protein load set for
that run, washed with the same buffer, and eluted by a step change to the elution buffer
at the pH set for that run. The pool was collected from a fixed optical density on the
ascending edge of the elution peak to the stop collect optical density set for that run on
the descending edge. The column was then stripped, sanitized and stored under SOP-2008.

The load material for every run was the neutralized pool of the low-pH viral inactivation
step, prepared from a single production campaign so that the input aggregate and host cell
protein burden would not vary between runs. Resin lot, packed bed height, buffer
composition, equilibration volume and wash volume were held at their platform values
throughout. These inputs are controlled by identity and release testing under SOP-2010 and
SOP-2008 and were not varied in the study.

## Analytical methods

@tbl-amv lists the validated methods used to measure the responses and the cleared
attributes. Pool aggregate was measured by size exclusion chromatography (SEC-HPLC) under
AMV-3011 and is reported as the percentage of high molecular weight species in the total
peak area. Pool host cell protein was measured by immunoassay (ELISA) under AMV-3012 and
is reported relative to the product mass. Residual DNA was measured by quantitative
polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) under AMV-3014 and leached Protein A by immunoassay under
AMV-3016. Step yield was calculated from the product mass in the pool relative to the
product mass loaded, each determined by ultraviolet absorbance.
```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=[], amvs=CEX_AMV_REFS))
```
: Validated analytical methods used in the study. {#tbl-amv}

The precision of these methods sets a floor on the variation the study can attribute to
the process. The host cell protein immunoassay (AMV-3012) is the least precise of the
four, at `{python} f"{amv_3012_precision:.1f}"` % coefficient of variation. Its share of the observed variance in the pool
host cell protein result is `{python} f"{amv_3012_var_frac:.2f}"`. The leached Protein A immunoassay has a precision of
`{python} f"{amv_3016_precision:.1f}"` % and a limit of quantitation of `{python} f"{amv_3016_loq:.2f}"` ppm, and method performance is summarized
in Appendix D.

## Sampling plan

The load was sampled once for each run and assayed for aggregate and host cell protein,
which made the burden entering the column known for every run. The elution pool was
sampled after collection was complete and assayed for aggregate, host cell protein,
residual DNA and leached Protein A. Protein concentration was measured on the load and on
the pool for the yield calculation. Runs were executed in randomized order within each
design.

The screening design contributed `{python} n_scr` runs and the response surface design `{python} n_rsm` runs,
of which `{python} cp_scr` and `{python} cp_rsm` respectively were centre-point replicates at the set-point
condition of every factor. Every run of both designs is reported, and no run was excluded
from any analysis.

## Statistical methods

Each factor was coded so that its set-point is 0 and the edges of its characterization
range are the coded levels −1 and +1. The set-point is the midpoint of the
characterization range for all four multivariate factors of this step, which makes the
centre point of both designs (the coded origin) the set-point condition of the step.
Analyses were run under SOP-1002 at a significance level of α = 0.05.

The screening data were fitted by ordinary least squares to a model containing the four
main effects and the six two-factor interactions. The effect of a term is reported as
twice its coded coefficient, which is the change in the response across the full
characterization range of that factor. The response surface data were fitted to the full
quadratic model in the same four factors, which adds the four squared terms. Model
adequacy was judged by the coefficient of determination, by its adjusted form, by the
predicted form computed from the prediction sum of squares, by the overall F test, and by
an analysis of variance that splits the residual into lack of fit and pure error and tests
the first against the second. A factor with no term significant at α = 0.05 in any model
is reported as having no detected effect, which is a statement about the ranges studied
and not about the parameter in general.

The screening design identifies which factors are active, while the response surface model
is the predictive model, from which every prediction, design space boundary and proven
acceptable range in this report is taken. The screening estimates are reported in §5.2 for
the directions and the relative sizes they establish, and are not used to predict.

Proven acceptable ranges were determined in two analyses for each attribute and parameter.
The first holds the other parameters at their set-points and scans the parameter of
interest across its characterization range on the fitted response surface. The second
varies the other parameters within their normal operating ranges by Monte-Carlo simulation
of the fitted model, including the residual variation of the model, and requires the
resulting 95 % predictive interval to remain inside the criterion. The second is the more
demanding of the two, and is the analysis that bounds the routine operating region.
Commercial-scale capability was estimated by simulating `{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches of the whole train
with every parameter varying inside its normal operating range, and is reported as a one
sided capability index against the drug substance criterion.

## Screening design

The screening study was a two-level full factorial in the four multivariate factors,
augmented with `{python} cp_scr` centre points, giving `{python} n_scr_fact` factorial runs and `{python} n_scr` runs in
total. The design estimates all four main effects and all six two-factor interactions, and
leaves `{python} dfres('screening', AGG)` residual degrees of freedom (Appendix A). A full factorial was used rather
than a fraction because four factors are few enough that no aliasing between a main effect
and a two-factor interaction is necessary, and because three of the four were expected to
interact. The centre points give a direct test for overall curvature and the pure error
term. The coded design matrix and the measured responses of the screening design are in
Appendix A.

## Response-surface design

The response surface study was a face centred central composite design in the same four
factors. It reuses the `{python} n_rsm_fact` factorial points, adds `{python} n_rsm_ax` axial points at the face
centres of the coded cube and `{python} cp_rsm` centre points, giving `{python} n_rsm` runs. Axial points at
the faces rather than beyond them keep every run inside the characterization range. No
prediction from the model therefore requires a setting the study did not visit. The design
supports the full quadratic model, which has `{python} npar('rsm', AGG)` terms and leaves `{python} dfres('rsm', AGG)` residual
degrees of freedom, of which `{python} FIT[('rsm', AGG)]['df_pe']` are pure error. The coded design matrix and the
measured responses of the response surface design are in Appendix B.

## Univariate assessment

Elution flow rate was assessed one at a time across `{python} f"{CFG.unit_op(UO).param('flow').prange[0]:g}"` to `{python} f"{CFG.unit_op(UO).param('flow').prange[1]:g}"` cm/hr with the other
parameters at their set-points. Flow rate sets the residence time during elution and
therefore the sharpness of the elution peak. However, over this range and at the particle
size of the resin the change in resolution is small. The assessment found no effect on
pool aggregate, pool host cell protein or step yield that would place the parameter in the
design space. It is classified as a general process parameter in §9 and is controlled at
its set-point by the pump under SOP-2010.

## Mechanistic interpretation

The directions of all four effects follow from the physical chemistry of a bind and elute
cation exchange separation, and the study confirms them.

Protein load acts on all three responses through one quantity (the fraction of the ligand
in use). As the column approaches its capacity the monomer and aggregate peaks broaden and
their overlap increases, a larger part of the aggregate front arrives inside the collected
pool, and pool aggregate rises. The same broadening loses monomer at both edges of the
pool, at the stop collect point and in the fraction cut away with the aggregate, and step
yield falls. At high load there is also less free ligand from which the wash can displace
the weakly bound host cell protein, more of it co-adsorbs with the antibody, and pool host
cell protein rises. Therefore, one physical quantity explains a positive load coefficient
on pool aggregate, a positive one on pool host cell protein and a negative one on step
yield, which is what @tbl-coef-agg and @tbl-coef-hcp show.

Elution buffer pH and elution stop collect act on the aggregate separation and on nothing
else. A higher elution pH reduces the net positive charge on the antibody and weakens its
binding. Monomer and aggregate then leave the column earlier and closer together, and the
resolution on which the separation depends is compressed. A later stop collect takes more
of the descending edge of the elution peak into the pool, and the aggregate elutes on that
edge. Neither parameter affects the load and wash phase, which is where host cell protein
is cleared, and neither has a significant coefficient in the pool host cell protein model.

All three interactions in the pool aggregate model are positive, which follows from the
same argument. Each pair of factors acts on the resolution or on the pool cut, and the
penalty of raising one is therefore larger when the other has already been raised. Raising
the elution pH at a high load moves an already broadened aggregate front into a pool that
is already collecting into the tail. The model puts the interaction of load with elution
pH at `{python} f"{co(AGG, 'AC'):+.3f}"` per coded unit, against a main effect of `{python} f"{co(AGG, 'A'):+.3f}"` for load. The practical
consequence is that the aggregate performance of the step cannot be read from any one
parameter. It is read from the corner of the operating region, which is why the design
space in §6 is stated as a region and not as four independent ranges.

Wash conductivity acts on host cell protein clearance alone, through the ionic strength
that shields the charge between the ligand and the weakly bound acidic species. A higher
conductivity displaces more of that population during the wash while the antibody, which
binds more strongly, stays adsorbed. Its interaction with protein load is negative, which
means the benefit of a higher wash conductivity is larger at high load than at low load.
That is expected, because a heavily loaded column carries more co-adsorbed host cell
protein for the wash to remove. Its interaction with elution buffer pH is also negative,
and the mechanism is the same population seen from the other end. Where the wash has
already stripped the weakly bound host cell protein, raising the elution pH releases
little further, and where it has not, the higher pH carries more of it into the pool.

Residual DNA and leached Protein A behaved as the mechanism predicts. Both are acidic or
strongly negatively charged at the operating pH, neither binds the sulfonate ligand, and
both were cleared in the load flow through at every condition of both designs. Clearance
was `{python} f"{dna_lrv:.1f}"` log₁₀ for residual DNA and `{python} f"{lpa_lrv:.1f}"` log₁₀ for leached Protein A, and neither
varied with any studied parameter across the ranges tested. Neither attribute constrains
the operating region of this step.

# Design space

The design space of this step is the region of the four multivariate parameters over which
the fitted response-surface models predict a pool that meets both in-process criteria,
which are `{python} f"{ipc_hi(AGG):g}"` % HMW for aggregate and `{python} f"{ipc_hi(HCP):.0f}"` ng/mg for host cell protein. The region
was evaluated on an even grid of `{python} f"{DS['n_points']:,}"` points over the characterized cube, of which
`{python} pct(DS['fraction'])` meet both criteria. Aggregate is the binding constraint and rejects `{python} pct(DS['per_response'][AGG])` of the
cube on its own, while host cell protein rejects `{python} pct(DS['per_response'][HCP])`.

The two constraints bind in different planes, which is why the region is stated as a
region. Aggregate is bounded from above by protein load, elution buffer pH and elution
stop collect acting together, and @fig-contour-agg shows the aggregate surface rising
towards the corner where load and elution pH are both high. Host cell protein is bounded
from below by wash conductivity and from above by protein load, and @fig-contour-hcp shows
its surface rising towards the corner where load is high and wash conductivity low.
Protein load appears in both boundaries, with opposite partners, and is the parameter that
carries the operating region.

Three nested regions are used in this report and they are not the same thing. The
characterization ranges in @tbl-params bound the knowledge space, which is the region the
study visited. The design space is the part of that region shown above to meet both
in-process criteria. The normal operating ranges in @tbl-params are the ranges the process
will be operated within at commercial scale, and lie inside the characterized ranges on
every parameter.

The normal operating ranges are not entirely inside the design space, a gap that is
reported here and not left to be inferred. Evaluated on the same fitted models over an
even grid across the normal operating ranges of the four parameters, `{python} pct(nor_ok_frac)` of that
smaller region meets both criteria. The part that does not is the corner at high protein
load with a high elution pH and a late stop collect, where the predicted pool aggregate
reaches `{python} f"{NOR_MAX[AGG]:.2f}"` % HMW against the in-process limit of `{python} f"{ipc_hi(AGG):g}"` %. Aggregate rejects `{python} pct(NOR_FAIL[AGG])`
of the normal operating region and host cell protein rejects `{python} pct(NOR_FAIL[HCP])`, the latter at the
opposite corner of low wash conductivity with high load.

Two things bound what that finding means, the first being that the in-process criteria are
not the drug substance criteria. The aggregate criterion sits an assurance factor of
`{python} f"{ipc_margin(AGG):g}"` below the drug substance criterion of `{python} f"{ds_hi(AGG):g}"` % HMW. Therefore, a pool predicted
at `{python} f"{NOR_MAX[AGG]:.2f}"` % HMW is above an internal control limit and is not a batch predicted to fail
specification. The second bound is that these are mean predictions of a mean-level model,
whose reliability at the edge of the shaded region is approximately half if the variation
around the mean is symmetric. For this reason the analysis in §7 replaces the mean by a 95
% predictive interval.

The consequence for change control is stated in ICH Q8 [@ichq8], where movement within the
design space is not a change from a regulatory filing perspective and movement outside it
is. Under ICH Q10 [@ichq10] any planned movement is still assessed under the
pharmaceutical quality system before it is made. Because part of the normal operating
range for protein load falls outside the region defined here, the control strategy in §10
holds the routine condition at the set-point and treats the pool aggregate result as the
in-process control that confirms the outcome of each batch.

# Proven acceptable ranges

@tbl-par gives the proven acceptable range of each response-surface factor against each
governed attribute. Two analyses are reported for each pair, of which the first holds the
other three parameters at their set-points and scans the parameter of interest across its
characterization range on the fitted model. The second varies the other three within their
normal operating ranges by Monte-Carlo simulation and requires the 95 % predictive
interval of the response to stay inside the criterion. The criterion column is the
in-process criterion of §2.2 in both cases, the basis being the same for every row of the
table (`{python} D.acceptance_basis(UO, AGG)`).
```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.par_table(UO))
```
: Proven acceptable ranges by governed attribute and parameter. {#tbl-par}

Two of the eight rows are bounded inside the characterization range under the first
analysis. Protein load is bounded at `{python} f"{par_sp(AGG, 'load', 1):.3g}"` g/L resin by the aggregate criterion, which
is an edge of failure inside a range the process could reach. Wash conductivity is bounded
from below at `{python} f"{par_sp(HCP, 'wash_cond', 0):.3g}"` mS/cm by the host cell protein criterion. The remaining six rows
extend across the whole characterization range at the set-point of the other parameters,
which means that no single parameter moved on its own leaves the criterion within the
range studied.

By contrast, the second analysis is more demanding, and every range narrows under it. For
aggregate, protein load narrows to `{python} f"{par_nor(AGG, 'load', 0):.3g}"` to `{python} f"{par_nor(AGG, 'load', 1):.3g}"` g/L resin, elution buffer pH to
`{python} f"{par_nor(AGG, 'elution_ph', 0):.3g}"` to `{python} f"{par_nor(AGG, 'elution_ph', 1):.3g}"` and elution stop collect to `{python} f"{par_nor(AGG, 'stop_collect', 0):.3g}"` to `{python} f"{par_nor(AGG, 'stop_collect', 1):.3g}"` OD on the descending
edge. For host cell protein, wash conductivity narrows to `{python} f"{par_nor(HCP, 'wash_cond', 0):.3g}"` to `{python} f"{par_nor(HCP, 'wash_cond', 1):.3g}"` mS/cm and
protein load to `{python} f"{par_nor(HCP, 'load', 0):.3g}"` to `{python} f"{par_nor(HCP, 'load', 1):.3g}"` g/L resin.

Comparing those ranges with the normal operating ranges in @tbl-params gives the same
finding as §6 from a different direction. The upper edge of the normal operating range for
protein load, at `{python} f"{NORB['load'][1]:g}"` g/L resin, lies above the proven acceptable range for aggregate
under the propagated analysis, which ends at `{python} f"{par_nor(AGG, 'load', 1):.3g}"` g/L resin. The lower edge of the
normal operating range for wash conductivity, at `{python} f"{NORB['wash_cond'][0]:g}"` mS/cm, lies below the proven
acceptable range for host cell protein, which starts at `{python} f"{par_nor(HCP, 'wash_cond', 0):.3g}"` mS/cm. The upper edges for
elution buffer pH and elution stop collect are likewise outside their propagated ranges by
a small margin. The set-point of every parameter is comfortably inside every proven
acceptable range. However, the propagated analysis does not support the edge of one
routine range taken with all three other parameters simultaneously at their own worst
positions.

@fig-par-agg shows the aggregate analysis against protein load (the governing parameter
for that attribute). The left panel is the analysis at the set-point and the right panel
the propagated one, with the acceptable region shaded and the normal operating range
marked. The predictive band in the right panel widens the curve enough to move the
boundary down by roughly a fifth of the characterization range, which is the size of the
penalty that simultaneous variation in the other three parameters carries.
```{python}
#| label: fig-par-agg
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range for pool aggregate against protein load, at set-point (left) and with the other parameters varying within their normal operating ranges (right)."
D.fig_par(UO, AGG, GOV[AGG])
plt.show()
```
@fig-par-hcp shows the host cell protein analysis against wash conductivity, which is its
governing parameter. The criterion binds from below rather than from above, because the
weakly bound host cell protein is displaced by ionic strength. A conductivity that is too
low leaves it on the column to elute with the product.
```{python}
#| label: fig-par-hcp
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range for pool host cell protein against wash conductivity, at set-point (left) and with the other parameters varying within their normal operating ranges (right)."
D.fig_par(UO, HCP, GOV[HCP])
plt.show()
```
@fig-par-agg-stop shows the aggregate analysis against elution stop collect, which is the
direct handle on the trade between aggregate clearance and yield. Stopping the collection
earlier lowers the pool aggregate and loses monomer in the tail, while stopping later does
the reverse. The step is operated at `{python} f"{SP['stop_collect']:g}"` OD on the descending edge, which sits inside
both analyses.
```{python}
#| label: fig-par-agg-stop
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range for pool aggregate against elution stop collect, at set-point (left) and with the other parameters varying within their normal operating ranges (right)."
D.fig_par(UO, AGG, "stop_collect")
plt.show()
```
Two limits apply to every range in @tbl-par. The first is that the ranges are univariate
statements about one parameter at a time and do not replace the multivariate region of §6,
because a combination of parameters each inside its own proven acceptable range can still
sit outside the region. The second is that each range stops at the edge of the
characterization range, and a row that extends across the whole range is a statement about
the range studied and not an unbounded one. Step yield carries no proven acceptable range
at all, because it is a process performance attribute with no quality criterion attached
to it. It is reported in §5 only for the effect of protein load on it.

# Process capability and robustness

@tbl-cap gives the commercial-scale capability of the four attributes this step governs,
estimated by simulating `{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches of the whole train with every parameter of every
step varying inside its normal operating range. The capability index is one sided in each
case, because all four attributes carry an upper limit only.
```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cap_for(CQA_KEYS))
```
: Commercial-scale capability of the attributes governed by the step. {#tbl-cap}

Aggregate has a capability of `{python} f"{cpk('aggregates_hmw'):.1f}"` against the drug substance criterion of `{python} f"{ds_hi(AGG):g}"` %
HMW, with a simulated mean of `{python} f"{capmean('aggregates_hmw'):.2f}"` % and a highest simulated batch of `{python} f"{capmax('aggregates_hmw'):.2f}"` %. Host
cell protein has a capability of `{python} f"{cpk('hcp'):.1f}"` and is the tightest of the four, with a simulated
mean of `{python} f"{capmean('hcp'):.1f}"` ng/mg against a criterion of `{python} f"{ds_hi(HCP):g}"` ng/mg. Residual DNA is at `{python} f"{cpk('residual_dna'):.1f}"`,
and leached Protein A at `{python} f"{cpk('leached_protein_a'):.0f}"`, a figure that should be read as a bound rather than as
an estimate, because the simulated mean of `{python} f"{capmean('leached_protein_a'):.3f}"` ppm lies well below the limit of
quantitation of the assay (`{python} f"{amv_3016_loq:.2f}"` ppm).

The capability of this step cannot be separated from the capability of the train for three
of these four attributes. Host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A are
cleared again at anion exchange chromatography, which reduces host cell protein a further
`{python} f"{aex_hcp_fold:.1f}"`-fold in the nominal process. The figures in @tbl-cap are therefore the outcome of
both steps together. Aggregate is the exception, because no step after cation exchange
changes it. The aggregate capability of the drug substance is therefore delivered by this
step. The only other input to it is the load the step receives from the low-pH
inactivation step (Step 6).

The simulation gives the same picture as §6 and §7 at the level of whole batches. All
`{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` simulated batches met the drug substance criterion for all four attributes.
However, `{python} pct(frac_over_ipc)` of them carried more aggregate than the in-process limit of `{python} f"{ipc_hi(AGG):g}"` %
HMW. That is the same small corner of the normal operating range that §6 identified, seen
as a batch frequency instead of as a volume of parameter space. The in-process limit is
doing what an in-process limit is for, which is to flag those batches for assessment while
the drug substance criterion is still met with the margin @tbl-cap reports.

Robustness at the level of a single parameter follows from the same models. Elution flow
rate has no detected effect on any response over its characterization range, which is
twice the width of its normal operating range, leaving the step robust to it. Wash
conductivity has no detected effect on pool aggregate or on step yield, and acts on host
cell protein alone. Elution buffer pH and elution stop collect have no detected effect on
pool host cell protein or on step yield, and act on aggregate alone. Protein load is the
only parameter that acts on all three responses.

The tightest capability of the A-Mab drug substance is `{python} f"{V['min_cpk']:.2f}"`, which belongs to a
cumulative viral clearance attribute that this step does not contribute to. That attribute
and its contributing steps are reported in PCR-008 and PCR-009 and consolidated in
PCMR-001.

# Parameter classification

Every parameter of the step was classified under SOP-4001 from the effects demonstrated in
§5 and from the risk of leaving the operating region during routine manufacture. The
classification of each is given in @tbl-params and the reasoning is below.

- Protein load was classified as a well controlled critical process parameter, because it
  has the largest effect on pool aggregate, on pool host cell protein and on step yield.
  It is the parameter that bounds the operating region from above. It is not a critical
  process parameter, because the load is set by weight from a measured protein
  concentration on a pooled and assayed intermediate, which leaves the risk of moving
  outside the range during a batch low.
- Wash conductivity was classified as a well controlled critical process parameter,
  because it is the governing parameter for pool host cell protein and bounds the
  operating region from below. It has no effect on pool aggregate or step yield. The
  buffer is released against a conductivity specification before use and is measured in
  line during the wash, which leaves the risk of an undetected excursion low.
- Elution buffer pH was classified as a well controlled critical process parameter,
  because it has the second largest effect on pool aggregate and interacts with protein
  load. It has no detected effect on the other two responses. Buffer pH is set at
  preparation, released before use and monitored at the column inlet, which makes it easy
  to hold inside a range that is narrow in absolute terms.
- Elution stop collect was classified as a well controlled critical process parameter,
  because it affects pool aggregate directly and is the handle that trades aggregate
  against yield. It is executed by the chromatography system against an optical density
  set-point on the descending edge of the peak, which is an automated decision on a
  continuously measured signal. The parameter is therefore well controlled by
  construction.
- Elution flow rate was classified as a general process parameter, because no effect on
  any response was detected over a characterization range twice the width of its normal
  operating range. The mechanism gives no reason to expect one at this particle size, and
  it is controlled at its set-point by the pump and monitored as a process performance
  parameter.

The step therefore carries `{python} n_wccpp` well controlled critical process parameters, `{python} n_gpp`
general process parameter and `{python} n_cpp` critical process parameters. No parameter of this
step was classified as critical, because every quality linked parameter is set on a
measured signal or on a released buffer and none of them can move quickly enough during a
batch to leave its range undetected. Across the whole characterization campaign the train
carries `{python} class_counts()['CPP']` critical process parameter, which is reported in PCMR-001.

# Contribution to the control strategy

The step contributes five elements to the control strategy for commercial manufacture.

The first element is the set of parameter ranges. The four quality linked parameters are
operated within the normal operating ranges of @tbl-params and are recorded in the batch
record. Protein load is the parameter that carries the operating region. However, §6 and
§7 both place the upper part of its normal operating range outside the region that the
propagated analysis supports. The routine target for load is therefore the set-point and
not the upper part of the range. A batch executed above `{python} f"{par_nor(AGG, 'load', 1):.3g}"` g/L resin is assessed
against the pool aggregate result before the material is released to the next step.

The second element is in-process monitoring of the two governed responses, in which pool
aggregate is measured on every batch by AMV-3011 against an in-process limit of `{python} f"{ipc_hi(AGG):g}"` %
HMW and pool host cell protein by AMV-3012 against `{python} f"{ipc_hi(HCP):.0f}"` ng/mg. Both limits are derived
in §2.2 and both carry an assurance factor below the point at which the drug substance
would be at risk. A result above either one triggers an assessment of the batch and not a
rejection of it. Aggregate is the more important of the two for this step, because it is
the last step that can reduce it.

The third element is the life-cycle control of the column, in which resin lot, packing
quality and the number of cycles are controlled under SOP-2008, and column efficiency is
verified by plate count and peak asymmetry against the acceptance criteria of that
procedure before use. The characterization in this report was executed on a column within
those criteria, making the operating ranges valid for a column that meets them. Resin
ageing was not a variable of this study and is managed by the resin life-cycle programme
rather than by a parameter range.

The fourth element is the control of the material entering the step, which is the
neutralized pool of the low-pH viral inactivation step (Step 6). The aggregate content of
that pool is an input this step does not control. The nominal load carries `{python} f"{agg_in:.2f}"` % HMW
and the step reduces it `{python} f"{agg_fold:.1f}"`-fold, which means that an increase in the incoming burden
consumes the same margin as an increase in protein load. The in-process limit on the
aggregate content of the viral inactivation pool, reported in PCR-006, is the control that
bounds this input.

The fifth element is release testing of the drug substance, in which aggregate, host cell
protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A are tested against the criteria in @tbl-cqa.
The capability of each is reported in §8, while the attributes this step clears but does
not set are also controlled at anion exchange chromatography (PCR-008). The viral safety
of the process rests on the low-pH inactivation, anion exchange and virus filtration steps
and not on this one. The contribution of this step to the overall control strategy is
consolidated in PCMR-001.

# Discussion

The step is now characterized over ranges two to three times wider than the ranges it will
be operated within, and shows the behaviour the physical chemistry predicts. Four
parameters were studied multivariately and all four separate cleanly by mechanism. Protein
load acts on every response through the fraction of the ligand in use. Elution buffer pH
and elution stop collect act on the aggregate separation and on nothing else, while wash
conductivity acts on host cell protein clearance and on nothing else. That separation is
what makes the operating region interpretable, because each boundary of it can be
attributed to a named physical cause and not only to a fitted coefficient.

Aggregate rather than host cell protein bounds this step, and that has a consequence for
the control strategy. Host cell protein is the attribute with the longer history of being
difficult at a polishing step. Moreover, it has the tightest capability of the four
attributes in @tbl-cap, at `{python} f"{cpk('hcp'):.1f}"`. However, it is cleared again downstream, while
aggregate is cleared here for the last time. The propagated proven acceptable ranges in §7
narrow faster for aggregate than for host cell protein. A step judged on host cell protein
alone would be given a wider operating region than the data supports.

Confidence in the scale-down model rests on three observations, the first being its
qualification against at-scale data under SOP-1001 on the input attributes, the output
attributes and the performance of the separation. The centre-point means of the response
surface design sit close to the values the nominal commercial process delivers, at `{python} f"{cvr(AGG, 'Mean'):.2f}"`
% HMW and `{python} f"{cvr(HCP, 'Mean'):.0f}"` ng/mg. The lack of fit test is not significant for any of the three
responses, which shows that the run to run spread of the model is large enough to contain
the residual of a quadratic surface fitted to it and that no systematic shape was missed.

Three limitations bound the claims made here. The first is that the models are mean-level
models, in which the predicted response at a point is a mean and the assurance that a
batch at that point meets the criterion is roughly half at the boundary of the region. For
this reason the propagated analysis in §7 governs the routine ranges, while the analysis
at the set-point is reported beside it and not in place of it. The models are also valid
only inside the characterization ranges, because no squared term reached significance and
a surface that is planar within a range gives no information about its shape beyond that
range. Finally, the design space has not been confirmed at scale at its edges. The
commercial process will be executed at the set-point during process performance
qualification, while the edges of the region rest on the qualified scale-down model.

Two deviations were recorded and both were retained, with the investigations reported in
§13, and neither changed a conclusion. The affected runs were retained in the analysis,
and each sits within `{python} f"{max(dev1_sr, dev2_sr):.1f}"` residual standard deviations of the value its model fits.
Neither run is influencing the fitted surfaces in a way that would change an effect
estimate or a boundary.

# Conclusions

The cation exchange polishing step has been characterized on a qualified scale-down model
over ranges wider than its intended operating ranges, and meets the five objectives of
§1.2. Protein load, elution buffer pH and elution stop collect govern the aggregate
content of the pool, wash conductivity and protein load govern the host cell protein
content, and protein load governs the step yield. Elution flow rate has no detected effect
on any of them.

The design space is the region of the four parameters over which both in-process criteria
are met, and covers `{python} pct(DS['fraction'])` of the characterized region, with aggregate as the binding
constraint. Proven acceptable ranges were established for each parameter against each
governed attribute in two analyses. The propagated analysis places the upper part of the
normal operating range for protein load, elution buffer pH and elution stop collect, and
the lower part of the range for wash conductivity, outside the supported region. The
routine condition is the set-point, which sits inside every range by a clear margin.

At commercial scale all `{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` simulated batches meet the drug substance criteria for the
four attributes this step governs, with a capability of `{python} f"{cpk('aggregates_hmw'):.1f}"` for aggregate and `{python} f"{cpk('hcp'):.1f}"`
for host cell protein, the tightest of the four. `{python} n_wccpp` parameters were classified as
well controlled critical process parameters and `{python} n_gpp` as a general process parameter,
with no critical process parameter at this step. The `{python} n_dev` recorded deviations were
investigated and retained, leaving the outcome of this step to be carried into the master
report PCMR-001 in support of Stage 2.

# Deviations from the plan

`{python} n_dev` deviations from PCP-007 were recorded during execution and are listed in @tbl-dev.
Both were detected after the affected run had been executed, both were investigated under
the site deviation procedure, and both were dispositioned as retained, which means the
affected run stayed in the reported analysis. No deviation invalidated a design and no
study was re-executed.
```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dev_register(DOC))
```
: Deviations recorded during execution. {#tbl-dev}

## DEV-007-01, expired load and wash buffer lot

Screening run `{python} dev_run('DEV-007-01')` was executed with a lot of Tris load and wash buffer, LOT-BUF-2287,
that had passed its expiry date of `{python} lot_buf_2287_expiry` before the run was performed. The lot was not
identified at preparation and the deviation was found in the documentation review after
the design had been executed. The root cause is that the expiry date was not verified when
the buffer was issued to the run, which is a control failure in the issuing step and not a
defect of the buffer itself.

The investigation followed SOP-2103, which authorises re-test of a retained sample when an
expiry deviation is raised. The retained sample of LOT-BUF-2287 was re-tested for the two
attributes that determine how the buffer behaves in this step. It returned a pH of `{python} f"{dev_007_01_retest_ph:.2f}"`
and a conductivity of `{python} f"{dev_007_01_retest_cond:.2f}"` mS/cm, both within the release specification the lot had met
when it was prepared, which shows that the buffer had not changed in the properties the
step depends on.

The impact on the study was assessed from the fitted screening model, because run `{python} dev_run('DEV-007-01')`
is a factorial corner run that carries weight in every effect estimate. Its measured
responses sit within `{python} f"{dev1_sr:.1f}"` residual standard deviations of the values the screening
model fits for that condition, across all three responses. A run that the model reproduces
to within its own residual spread is not distorting the effect estimates. The direction
and the significance of every screening effect in §5.2 are unchanged whether the run is
treated as conforming or not. The run was retained, with the deviation closed by a
corrective action on the buffer issuing step under SOP-2103.

## DEV-007-02, column inlet temperature excursion

During response surface run `{python} dev_run('DEV-007-02')` the column inlet temperature rose to `{python} f"{dev_007_02_tmax:.1f}"` °C and
stayed above the controlled range for `{python} dev_007_02_duration` minutes, which covers the load and part of
the wash phase of that run. The excursion was found in the equipment history review of
EQ-CHR-118 (the temperature-controlled chromatography chamber) and not during the run. The
root cause was a drift of the chamber controller. The chamber itself was within its
calibration at execution, with calibration next due on `{python} eq_chr_118_cal_due`, which shows that the drift
was in the controller set-point and not in the measurement.

Temperature affects a cation exchange separation through the viscosity of the mobile phase
and through the binding equilibrium, with a higher temperature sharpening the peaks
slightly and weakening binding slightly. Both would act on the aggregate result of the
affected run, which is why the impact was assessed on that response. Three verification
runs were executed at the condition of run `{python} dev_run('DEV-007-02')` with the chamber under control. The
pools were assayed by AMV-3221, a verification qualified size exclusion method with a
precision of `{python} f"{amv_3221_precision:.1f}"` % and a limit of quantitation of `{python} f"{amv_3221_loq:.2f}"` % HMW (Appendix D). On
`{python} dev_007_02_ver_n` runs that precision gives a 95 % confidence half-width on the mean of `{python} f"{dev_007_02_ci_hw:.2f}"` %
relative, which is the resolution with which the verification can detect a shift.

No shift larger than that resolution was found between the affected run and the
verification runs. The measured responses of run `{python} dev_run('DEV-007-02')` also sit within `{python} f"{dev2_sr:.1f}"` residual
standard deviations of the values the response surface model fits for that condition,
across all three responses. The run is consistent with the surface fitted to the other
`{python} (n_rsm - 1)` runs of the design. The run was retained, the controller was recalibrated and the
chamber set-point was added to the pre-run verification checklist for the step under
SOP-2010.

The two deviations are independent. One is a material control failure detected in
documentation review and the other an equipment control failure detected in equipment
history review. They affect different designs and different runs, and neither shares a
root cause with the other. Neither affects the design space of §6, the proven acceptable
ranges of §7 or the classification of §9.
